# Binary Deal‑Check / Stage‑Exit Checklist  
**Yes/no inspection for every stage. Keep deals on track. Exit when the signal is clear.**

---

## Who it's for  
Tiny enablement teams (1–3 people) running pipeline hygiene and stage gating in pre-IPO orgs.

---

## Artifact Body  

| Stage | Key Criteria | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | Notes |
|-------|--------------|--------|-------|-------|
| **Prospecting** | ICP match confirmed | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Outreach cadence active | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Contact made | ☐ | ☐ | |
| **Qualification** | Budget exists | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Authority mapped | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Need validated | ☐ | ☐ | |
| **Discovery** | Pain articulated by buyer | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Solution fit discussed | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Timeline set | ☐ | ☐ | |
| **Proposal** | Proposal delivered | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Value confirmed by champion | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Pricing agreed in principle | ☐ | ☐ | |
| **Negotiation** | Objections resolved | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Legal/procurement engaged | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Close date committed | ☐ | ☐ | |
| **Closed** | Contract signed | ☐ | ☐ | |
| | Onboarding scheduled | ☐ | ☐ | |

### Stage‑Exit Rule  
- **Any ❌ No = flag for exit.**

2. **Flag** deal in CRM.  
3. **Log** exit reason or next step in Notes.

1. **Pull** open deals in CRM.  
2. **Run** binary check on each stage.  
3. **Flag** exits; ping manager if pattern emerges.

# CRO AI‑Savings Reinvestment Scorecard

**Prove AI bought you time, then prove you spent it on coaching, deals, and selling.**

---

## Who it's for

CROs, Sales Ops, Enablement Leads running 1–3 person teams who want a single-page checklist to turn saved hours into revenue motion — and catch seat‑creep before it starts.

---

## The Scorecard

Copy this table. Fill it weekly. Mark the gap, assign the owner, set the date.

| **Category**       | **AI‑Saved Hours** | **Reinvested Hours** | **Gap** | **Action**                          | **Owner** | **Due** |
|--------------------|--------------------|----------------------|---------|-------------------------------------|-----------|---------|
| Coaching           |                    |                      |         |                                     |           |         |
| Deal Inspection    |                    |                      |         |                                     |           |         |
| Selling Block      |                    |                      |         |                                     |           |         |
| **Total**          |                    |                      |         |                                     |           |         |

**How to fill it:**  
- **AI‑Saved Hours:** Pull from your AI tool's dashboard or ask your ops lead for last week's aggregate.  
- **Reinvested Hours:** Calendar proof — actual hours managers logged in coaching sessions, deal reviews, or selling time.  
- **Gap:** Subtract reinvested from saved. Positive gap = time leaked.  
- **Action:** "Schedule 2 coaching slots" or "Block Friday afternoon for deals."  
- **Owner / Due:** Name + next Monday.

**EXAMPLE**: If AI saved 12 hours (EXAMPLE) and you logged 7 coaching hours, gap = 5 hours. Action: "Add 5 hours of deal‑review blocks by Friday." Owner: Sales Ops. Due: 2025‑05‑09.

---

## Monday Motion (3 Steps)

1. **Pull last week's AI‑saved hours** — export or screengrab from your tool.  
2. **Log reinvested hours** — check calendars, coaching notes, deal‑review agendas. Fill the table.  
3. **Decide on seat purchase**:  
   - **If total gap > 10 hours (EXAMPLE):** Hold the seat request. Fix the leak first.  
   - **If gap ≤ 3 hours (EXAMPLE) for two weeks straight:** Approve the seat.

---

## Related CTAs

- [/assessment](/assessment) — Baseline your current AI + enablement operating model  
- [/start-here](/start-here) — Framework overview  
- [/enabling-leaders/enabling-managers](/enabling-leaders/enabling-managers) — Manager coaching structure  
- [/enabling-leaders/enablement-operating-model](/enabling-leaders/enablement-operating-model) — Weekly rhythm that makes reinvestment automatic  
- [/build-the-system](/build-the-system) — Turn this scorecard into a repeatable operating motion

---

**Disclosure:** All hours, gaps, and percentages in this guide are illustrative (EXAMPLE) and not based on third‑party research. Use your own calendar and AI‑tool data to fill the scorecard.

# Starter Agent Policy Catalog **Who it's for** Revenue operator or enablement manager at a 1–3 person pre‑IPO team who needs to know *exactly* which agents write to the CRM, when a human must review, and how to hand the policy off intact. --- ## The catalog | Use Case | Data Source | CRM Truth | Signal Feed | Human Gate? | Write Rule | |----------|-------------|-----------|-------------|-------------|------------| | Lead capture | Form POST | Lead record | Scoring model | No | `lead.owner = agent`
`lead.status = "New"` | | Opportunity qual | Opp form | Opp record | Stage history | **Yes** | `if stage == "Qualified"`
` lead.status = "Qualified"` | | Deal close | Close form | Deal record | Won value | **Yes** | `if deal.value > 0`
` opp.status = "Closed Won"` | | Account refresh | Account sync | Account record | Health snapshot | No | `account.owner = agent`
`account.status = "Active"` | > **Mark each yes/no now:** > 1. Does your CRM schema match the field names in column six? > 2. Do you have write credentials scoped to *only* those fields? > 3. Can a manager approve the human‑gate rows in Slack in under two minutes? > 4. Is the YAML below committed to version control? > 5. Does one person own breaking changes to this catalog? > 6. Can the next ops hire read this table and ship a policy update on day one? --- ## Sample YAML ```yaml # agent_policies.yml – EXAMPLE VALUES ONLY policies: - name: lead_capture data_source: lead_form crm_truth: lead_db signal_feed: lead_scoring human_gate: false write_rules: - "lead.owner = agent" - "lead.status = 'New'" - name: opportunity_qual data_source: opp_form crm_truth: opp_db signal_feed: stage_history human_gate: true write_rules: - "if (opp.stage == 'Qualified') { lead.status = 'Qualified' }" - name: deal_close data_source: close_form crm_truth: deal_db signal_feed: won_value human_gate: true write_rules: - "if (deal.value > 0) { opp.status = 'Closed Won' }" ``` *Numbers, field names, and threshold logic are EXAMPLE placeholders.* --- ## Monday Motion 1. **Audit** – Open the YAML; confirm each policy still matches production CRM field names. 2. **Flag** – If a human‑gate policy fired more than *EXAMPLE: 10 times* last week, add a pre‑filter rule. 3. **Commit** – Push the updated YAML and tag the ops channel so the next sprint inherits clean policy. --- ## Related - [Assessment](/assessment) - [Start Here](/start-here) - [Enabling Managers](/enabling-leaders/enabling-managers) - [Enablement Operating Model](/enabling-leaders/enablement-operating-model) - [Build the System](/build-the-system) --- **Disclosure** This catalog is a starting template. # Correction Loop Ritual  
**Challenge This Page** – Keep your field‑guide pages fresh and accurate.  
A quick, weekly ritual for 1‑3 enablement teammates.

---

## Who it’s for  
- Enablement Leads  
- Enablement Managers  
- Enablement Ops

## Ritual Checklist

| Step | Action | Owner | Frequency | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|-----------|-------|
| **1️⃣ Flag** | Scan the page for stale claims, broken links, or outdated data. | 1–3 team members | Weekly | Use the “Stale Claim” flag in the page’s comment section. |
| **2️⃣ Verify** | Cross‑check flagged items against the latest source (product docs, data dashboards, or stakeholder input). | 1–3 team members | Weekly | If you’re unsure, ping the relevant product owner. |
| **3️⃣ Patch** | Update the content, replace broken links, or add new data. Commit the change and add a brief note in the revision history. | 1–3 team members | Weekly | Keep the patch concise—focus on the specific claim, not the whole page. |
| **4️⃣ Review** | Quick peer‑review of the patch to catch typos or formatting drift. | 1–3 team members | Weekly | One person does the review; the other two approve. |

# 30‑60‑90 Enablement Lead Playbook **A concise, operating‑system‑first roadmap for solo enablement leaders in pre‑IPO teams. Build systems, not content, and protect your calendar.** --- ## Who it’s for **Solo Enablement Lead** at a pre‑IPO, tiny‑team company (1‑3 people). You’re the only person pulling the enablement engine together—no content factory, just a lean operating system. --- ## 30‑60‑90 Day Field Guide | Phase | Objectives | Outcomes | Calendar Protections | What to Refuse | Key Actions | |-------|------------|----------|----------------------|----------------|-------------| | **30 days** | 1. Map the current state
2. Identify quick‑wins | • Baseline inventory of tools, docs, and gaps
• 3 quick‑win system tweaks | • 1 h “Discovery” block every Monday
• 30 min “Status” check‑in with CEO | • “Content‑heavy” workshops
• Unplanned ad‑hoc requests | • Conduct a 1‑hour “State‑of‑Enablement” walk‑through with each team member
• Create a shared “Enablement Map” (tool‑list + workflow diagram)
• Draft a 30‑day “System Sprint” backlog | | **60 days** | 1. Build core operating system
2. Automate repetitive tasks | • 2 core systems in place (e.g., onboarding pipeline, knowledge‑base workflow)
• 20 % reduction in manual hand‑offs | • 2 h “System Design” block every Tuesday
• 15 min “Refine” review each Friday | • “Show‑and‑tell” demos without impact
• “All‑hands” meetings that don’t move the needle | • Design and launch the onboarding pipeline (templates, checklists, automation triggers)
• Implement a knowledge‑base workflow (tagging, search, review cadence)
• Set up a weekly “System Health” dashboard | | **90 days** | 1. Scale systems
2. Embed culture | • Systems adopted by 100 % of team
• Enablement metrics (time‑to‑competence, task‑completion) in place | • 1 h “Scale” block every Thursday
• 30 min “Celebrate” session each month | • “Feature‑first” mindset
• “One‑off” fixes that break the system | • Roll out system‑wide adoption training
